ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — George Washington Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care for painful, loose dentures that make eating and speaking difficult, with weight loss: oral examination and oral cancer screening, nutrition screening, the evaluation of weight loss, and a prosthodontic referral. Concerns: Eating hurts and takes a long time, he has given up many foods, and he has lost weight; His dentures move and click when he speaks in public and push out his lower lip; He wants dentures that stay in place and do not hurt, without long absences from work. [S]

tr.td: Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes
Chest radiograph, two views: right lower lobe consolidation without effusion or cavity
Panoramic radiograph: edentulous jaws without retained roots, cysts or other bony lesion; mandibular bone height about 14 mm at the symphysis; mental foramina close to the crest of the lower ridge
Relief of the lower denture flange over the healed ulcer sites and a chairside tissue-conditioning reline of the old lower denture until the new dentures are made
Cone beam CT of the mandible for implant planning: bone about 6 mm wide and 13 to 14 mm high in both canine regions, enough for two standard implants without bone grafting
Delivery of new upper and lower complete dentures, with the lower denture designed for later conversion to an implant overdenture
Placement of two endosseous implants (4.1 x 10 mm) in the lower canine regions, with good primary stability and no bone graft; lower denture relieved and soft-lined over the implants
Connection of stud attachments to the two implants and pick-up of the attachment housings into the lower denture, converting it to an implant-retained overdenture

tr.td: Establishing primary care for painful, loose dentures that make eating and speaking difficult, with weight loss: oral examination and oral cancer screening, nutrition screening, the evaluation of weight loss, and a prosthodontic referral
Two-week review, seen the same day by prosthodontics: the oral ulcers, the diagnosis and the plan for new dentures and a two-implant lower overdenture
Twelve-week review: new complete dentures six weeks in use, three weeks after two lower implants were placed; eating, speech, weight and healing
Clinical resolution review two weeks after outpatient pneumonia, with the implant healing and weight
Six-month review: the implant-retained lower overdenture in use for three weeks; chewing, speech, nutrition and long-term maintenance
Same-day sick visit for fever, cough and chest pain

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Oral examination and oral cancer screening at every visit: lips, cheeks, tongue, floor of mouth, palate, ridges and neck nodes; a mouth ulcer under a denture is re-examined two weeks after the denture is relieved or left out, and biopsied if it has not healed
Prosthodontics consultation to diagnose the edentulous jaws and denture problems, review the ulcers, and plan new dentures and implant options
Comfort until the consultation: lower denture out except at meals, a soft diet that still includes protein, acetaminophen as needed, warm salt-water rinses, no denture adhesive on the ulcers

Nutrition and weight: MNA-SF at intake and on review, weight at every visit, a high-protein soft diet with an oral nutritional supplement twice a day until chewing is restored, and a check of blood count, metabolic panel, albumin, hemoglobin A1c, TSH and vitamin B12 for other causes of weight loss

New complete dentures: upper conventional denture and a lower denture designed to be converted to an implant overdenture, with a tissue-conditioning reline of the old lower denture until delivery, and adjustment visits

Mandibular two-implant overdenture as the first-choice standard: cone beam CT, two implants in the canine regions with amoxicillin 2 g one hour before surgery and chlorhexidine rinses for two weeks, the denture relieved and soft-lined over the implants, and stud attachments connected after about three months of healing
Denture care: clean the dentures daily with a soft brush and a non-abrasive cleanser, keep them out overnight in water, clean the ridges and tongue, and see the prosthodontist each year
Speech with new dentures: reading aloud each day, practice of the sounds that change with denture position, and a speech-language assessment if speech is not clear by six weeks

Cardiovascular risk: blood pressure, lipids and diabetes screening at the preventive visit; tooth loss is recorded as associated with cardiovascular disease, not as a proven cause, and does not change his risk estimate
Oral ulcers healed within two weeks of relieving the denture, without need for a biopsy
Both ulcers healed at two weeks; no biopsy needed
New complete dentures that are comfortable and stable for eating and speaking
Delivered six weeks before the twelve-week review; one adjustment; no sore spots now
A two-implant lower overdenture in function
Two implants integrated; stud attachments connected three weeks before the six-month review
Regain weight and a normal nutrition screen
Weight 92.4 to 94.8 kg; MNA-SF 10 to 12; albumin 3.7 to 4.1 g/dL
Speak in public without the lower denture moving
No lifting or clicking during speeches since the attachments were connected

list.item: Independent in all activities. Chewing is slow and painful; he rates his chewing ability 3 out of 10. The lower denture lifts when he speaks and the upper clicks, so he speaks carefully and briefly in public; he is self-conscious that the dentures push out his lower lip [S]

Oral examination by the primary clinician: no natural teeth; upper and lower complete dentures with worn acrylic teeth, a loose lower denture that rocks on a flat ridge, and a closed bite; two shallow ulcers, about 4 and 6 mm, in the lower left buccal sulcus under the denture flange, tender, with a clean yellow base and no induration; palate pink, without redness under the upper denture; tongue, floor of mouth, lips and cheeks otherwise normal; no neck lymph nodes. Nutrition screen: MNA-SF 10 of 14, at risk of malnutrition [S]
Alert, reserved and dignified; speaks slowly and with care; mood frustrated by the dentures but otherwise steady; PHQ-2 1 [S]
